subject: Bridge package proposal — cost-share, term reset & SLA add-on for Q4 renewal
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@sparkmetrics.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ken.lopez@sparkmetrics.com, procurement@sparkmetrics.com
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal thoughts + tight budget window

Vanessa —

Quick note following our renewal check-in: leadership is supportive of keeping Redwood but they have a constrained Q4 budget and need a stronger cost justification. They asked for a bridge package we can commit to for six months: modest discount, a term reset to align with their fiscal year, and an SLA add-on for availability during peak processing windows.

Can you share what flexibility exists? Procurement would prefer any concessions to be time-limited and to include a clearly documented SLA credit schedule. Attaching our internal summary (for your reference).

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Patel
VP, Cloud Analytics — SparkMetrics
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@sparkmetrics.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal thoughts + tight budget window

Aisha —

Appreciate the context and the timeline. High level: we can put together a 6-month bridge package that includes a temporary 18% ARR credit (applied over the first three billing cycles), a 12-month term reset to align with your FY, and an SLA addendum guaranteeing 99.6% monthly availability during scheduled peak windows with a defined credit matrix.

Before I commit this to legal and finance I need a quick OK from my leadership for the cost-share/credit quantum and explicit signoff that the term reset is limited to the one-cycle you requested. Looping in Vivek and Ben to weigh in on exec approval and any pricing guardrails.

Proposed next step: brief exec review this afternoon, then I can send a redlined term sheet and SLA addendum for procurement.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior AM, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal thoughts + tight budget window

Vanessa / Ben —

Thanks for the heads-up. Key considerations from the deal desk:
- 18% credit applied up-front is within range but should be offset by a modest usage/commit uplift tied to the term reset.
- SLA add-on ok if the credit matrix caps liability at one monthly credit per rolling 30-day period; we should avoid open-ended penalties.
- Legal will need the redline to confirm indemnity and data clauses remain unchanged.

I can greenlight this if we capture a minimum committed spend increase of 10% YoY post-reset and a signed DocuSign within 5 business days of the term sheet. If SparkMetrics can't meet those, we should keep the concession smaller (12%).

Vivek
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@sparkmetrics.com>
Cc: ken.lopez@sparkmetrics.com, procurement@sparkmetrics.com, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 13:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal thoughts + tight budget window

Aisha —

Thanks — quick update from my side after internal sync: we can move forward with a conditional bridge package as follows:
- 15% one-time credit applied across first two invoices (cost-share with Redwood covering the remainder)
- 12-month term reset to align your contract anniversary to 01/01/2029
- SLA addendum guaranteeing 99.6% during peak windows with a capped credit of 25% of monthly fees per incident, max one incident credit per 30 days

Conditions: signed DocuSign within 5 business days and a written commitment to a 10% spend uptick after reset. If SparkMetrics cannot meet those, revised offer drops to 10% credit and no term reset.

Attaching a draft term sheet and SLA addendum for review.

Best,
Vanessa
From: Ken Lopez <ken.lopez@sparkmetrics.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, aisha.patel@sparkmetrics.com
Cc: procurement@sparkmetrics.com
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal thoughts + tight budget window

Vanessa / Team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Procurement wants to see the exact DocuSign packet and the legal redlines before they commit to the 5-day turnaround. Can you also confirm whether the credit applies before taxes and whether the SLA credit is redeemable as a cash refund or only as service credits?

We are running this through finance today; I’ll get back by COB tomorrow.

—Ken
Ken Lopez
Head of Procurement — SparkMetrics
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: aisha.patel@sparkmetrics.com, ken.lopez@sparkmetrics.com, procurement@sparkmetrics.com
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Bridge package proposal — cost-share, term reset & SLA add-on for Q4 renewal

Folks —

Legal reviewed the redline. Two quick asks before I sign off to DocuSign:
1) Make the SLA credit explicitly service-credit only (no cash refunds).
2) Add an expiry clause for the term reset: it reverts to the prior anniversary if post-reset committed spend < 10% uplift in the next 12 months.

If those two items are included I will authorize the DocuSign packet to be sent to SparkMetrics procurement. Vanessa — please confirm and I’ll route.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Deal Desk — Redwood Inference
